newsitem.title: UK: Hambros no longer adviser to Galileo, Lanica.
newsitem.headline: Hambros no longer adviser to Galileo, Lanica.

text.p: Investment bank Hambros Plc said on Monday it was no longer acting as financial advisers to Andrew Regan's Galileo and Lanica Trust.

Hambros, which offered an unreserved apology to the Co-Operative Wholesale Society (CWS) over its conduct when advising Regan's Galileo in its attempt to takeover the CWS, also said that having consulted its regulators, it had instructed solicitors Norton Rose to conduct an enquiry on its behalf.

CWS earlier said it had dropped legal proceedings against Hambros after chairman Sir Chips Keswick wrote to CWS offering an unreserved apology over its conduct. Keswick wrote that the judgement exercised by Hambros "fell well below our standards and those which you are entitled to expect from us".
CWS had originally said it would sue the bank because it had "acted in breach of an equitable obligation of confidentiality to CWS".

Galileo's hostile 1.2 billion pound ($1.9 billion) bid for CWS collapsed last week after CWS took legal action to prevent the use of the information leaked to entrepreneur Regan by CWS executives and after the withdrawal of key financial backing.

CWS, which attacked Hambros throughout the saga and sought explanations for its conduct on several occasions, had said Hambros could have no credible grounds for believing Regan had obtained the documents about CWS legitimately. ($ = 0.616 British Pounds)
